newsitem.title: UK: Enterprise suspends Nelson oilfield to remove bomb.
newsitem.headline: Enterprise suspends Nelson oilfield to remove bomb.

text.p: British oil explorer Enterprise Oil said on Friday it was suspending production from its North Sea Nelson oilfield to remove and dispose an unexploded World War II bomb found on the seabed next to the field's export pipeline.
Enterprise said the 160,000 barrel a day (bpd) field would be suspended for 3-5 days in an operation expected to take place in the next 10 days.
"With the assistance of the Royal Navy and other experts we are implementing the best and safest course of action for the ordance's disposal," Enterprise general manager of U.K. operations said.
The company said it had been assured by Royal Navy and Ministry of Defence experts that the bomb presented only a "minimal risk."

It was detected during a routine survey lying three meters from the pipeline in 100 meters of water some eight kilometers (five miles) form the Nelson platform and three kilometers from British Petroleum's Forties field Echo platform.
The company said it presumed fishing activity had snagged the device and moved it close to the line.
It would be moved and disposed of by specialist contractors using a remote operated vehicle.
Nelson supplies crude as part of the Forties network to Cruden Bay in Scotland.
Enterprise said the operation will have no impact on crude supplies from other fields using the Forties system.
